title: Binary length-12 covering codes of radius three
statement: Determine K_2(12,3), the smallest size of a set C in {0,...,1}^12 such that every word has Hamming distance at most 3 from some member of C. No linearity or symmetry restriction is imposed. The inspected sources report 19 <= K_2(12,3) <= 28; a certified improvement of either bound is a meaningful partial result.
status_basis: The most recent located primary bounds leave the interval [19,28] nontrivial. A targeted search for these parameters and subsequent improvements did not locate an exact value. This is a source-based gap, not an exhaustive certification of open status.
plain_summary: Choose as few length-12 words over a 2-symbol alphabet as possible so that every possible word lies within 3 symbol changes of one chosen word. Any smaller verified cover improves a concrete finite bound.
assumptions: The alphabet is {0,...,1}, with ordinary Hamming distance: the number of unequal coordinates.
The code is an arbitrary set, with no repeated words. Linear, additive and orbit-union constructions are optional search restrictions, not assumptions of the problem.
Covering radius means at most the stated radius; the task is not a packing or minimum-distance problem.
scope: The exact finite parameter K_2(12,3). A proposed first milestone is a code with at most 27 words. This choice of milestone and the resource ceiling below are curator proposals, pending review; they are not a separate conjecture attributed to the source.
target: Find and independently verify a cover of size at most 27, or obtain a rigorously certified improvement of the lower bound 19. Matching bounds would determine K_2(12,3); a one-sided improvement alone would not.
success_criteria: For a constructive improvement, provide a machine-readable list of at most 27 distinct words and a separate exhaustive coverage checker.
For a lower-bound improvement, supply a mathematical proof or independently checkable exact certificate valid for all unrestricted codes.
Record the achieved bound and its assumptions. A failed search, an infeasible restricted ansatz or a timeout is not a lower bound.
Recheck later literature before calling any improvement new.
known_results: The cited table or proposition reports 19 <= K_2(12,3) <= 28. These are literature claims, not bounds established by this project.
The lower endpoint comes from the semidefinite bounds in SRC-CODE-201; the table also records an existing construction for the upper endpoint.
prerequisites: Certificate checking and basic computational reproducibility
significance: A small covering-code gap offers a concrete research output with an independently inspectable witness. The main value is an improved bound or construction principle, not the mere completion of a search.

relations.explanation: Shares the covering-set formulation and exact witness checker; the parameter instances remain distinct mathematical questions.

requirements.data: Generate the 4,096 words directly. Existing code constructions can be starting points if their provenance and version are recorded; no external empirical dataset is needed.
requirements.compute: A direct witness check for 27 codewords uses at most 1,327,104 coordinate comparisons. This is an operation bound, not a measured runtime. A direct binary set-cover formulation has 4,096 variables and 4,096 covering constraints. Proposed initial ceiling: 4 CPU-hours and 8 GiB RAM, stopping sooner on a verified improvement. This is a curator-chosen exploration cap, not an estimate of the resources needed to solve the problem; no run or cost measurement has been made.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Finite combinatorics with exact Hamming distance. No model of physical noise or untested empirical assumption is required.

ai_assessment.rationale: An explicit finite witness is cheap to inspect and the target is precise, making bounded construction search a reasonable first trial. The search itself may still be difficult.

clarity.reason: A finite Hamming space, radius and cardinality determine the question exactly.

decomposability.reason: Constructive upper-bound work can be separated from lower bounds and exact optimality.

methods.reason: Set covering, local search, symmetry and exact optimization provide concrete tools; selecting an effective strategy remains research.

search_or_symbolic.reason: A code is a finite list and each Hamming ball has an exact bitset representation.

checkability.reason: A proposed upper-bound witness can be checked over all 4,096 words using integer operations.

expertise.reason: A construction checker is elementary; avoiding invalid symmetry restrictions and certifying lower bounds requires coding or optimization expertise.

significance.reason: An improved table entry is a modest, specific contribution; transferable constructions would have wider value.

verification_difficulty.reason: Low for an explicit covering witness; substantially higher for a nonexistence or optimality proof.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model has been evaluated on this task. A small universe and an inexpensive witness checker do not imply that a better cover is easy to find or exists at the selected target size.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes a tool-using model able to implement finite search and integer checkers, with human review of problem encoding and novelty.

methods: Represent each possible center by its exact Hamming-ball bitset.
Use local replacement, tabu search or exact set-cover encodings with a declared cardinality target.
Explore coordinate and symbol symmetries, documenting which restrictions may exclude valid codes.
For lower bounds, investigate exact combinatorial arguments or rigorously certified optimization duals.
obstacles: The feasible space of code subsets is enormous despite the small space of words.
Greedy or local search can stall at the known bound.
An orbit restriction can hide asymmetric improvements.
Numerical SDP output alone is insufficient as a new exact lower-bound certificate.

steps: Refresh the parameter-specific literature and record the exact source versions.
Validate the alphabet, word lengths, distinctness and claimed code size.
Independently enumerate every one of the 4,096 words and check distance to the submitted code. Record any uncovered word as a counterexample to the claimed cover.
Use a separately written checker and save the submitted witness with a content hash.
For nonexistence claims, audit encoding completeness, all symmetry reductions and the complete proof certificate; a solver status alone is insufficient.
Obtain human review of correctness and a separate comparison with the literature for novelty.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Low to moderate for an explicit upper-bound witness. High for unrestricted lower bounds or exact optimality.
validation.statement_alignment: The checker must test covering, not packing, in the full unrestricted Hamming space. Properties of one additive or symmetric code family do not settle the unrestricted minimum.

known_attempts: The inspected papers report computational bounds or constructions. Their reported runs are external research records and have not been repeated or used as AI benchmark results here.
unresolved_checks: Confirm that no later construction or lower-bound improvement changes this exact parameter cell.
Audit the source lower-bound certificate if it is needed in a future proof of optimality.
Retrieve and independently validate any published starting construction before relying on it.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: A finite witness proves its stated covering bound only after exact checking; optimality needs a separate unrestricted lower bound.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No empirical claim is involved. Heuristic success rates and AI performance are unknown.

difficulty.basis: Discovery and optimality remain difficult; witness verification is much easier than finding a better code.

correctness.basis: No new code or proof has been produced by this project.
